prompts:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: transparent equipment-rack overlay sprite for the existing isometric monster deployment floor tile.
Image 1: the newly designed purple-and-brass monster deployment tile, design and palette reference / edit source. Image 2: the game's skeleton guard, art-style reference only, do NOT copy a living guard.
Transform the first image into a SEPARATE MATCHING ARMOR RACK that will be composited on top of that tile in the game. Output the rack ONLY; completely remove the floor tile, background and floor shadow from this output. This is an EMPTY equipment stand for a skeleton monster, not an actual monster or person.
Subject: a small sturdy dark walnut wooden T-shaped armor stand with two short splayed support feet. A very readable ivory skull-shaped empty helmet with dark empty eye openings rests on the top peg. One pair of chunky aged-brass / dark-iron shoulder pauldrons hangs on the crossbar. A small tattered muted-purple tabard hangs from the crossbar behind an obvious visible vertical wooden post. A small round bronze-rim shield leans against one side. Keep the center clearly wooden / empty, no ribcage, no body, no hands, no legs, no face or eyes inside the helmet, no spear or weapons. It must read as an armor stand WAITING FOR A MONSTER to occupy its post.
Style: match the supplied cute hand-painted softly rendered 3D fantasy dungeon assets. Warm ivory helmet and golden brass shoulder edges should stay readable on a dark dungeon at 65 screen pixels tall. Broad simplified forms; subtle wear, no photorealism. Isometric orthographic 2:1 ground-plane perspective, facing the same viewer-facing direction as the skeleton reference; warm upper-left key light. No exaggerated glow.
Composition: one complete isolated rack, centered with 12 percent padding all sides on a transparent square canvas. The little wooden feet clearly define its ground contact. At runtime the rack is shorter than the skeleton guard, about 75 percent of its height. Output genuinely transparent alpha, no tile or platform, no shadow outside the rack, no text, no watermarks, no frame.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target: the supplied transparent monster armor-rack sprite.
Primary request: add a slightly broken, battered, awaiting-repair feeling to this exact armor stand. Keep it recognizably the same rack, same composition, same scale, same isometric direction, same warm painterly 3D style, same violet cloth and brass/dark iron palette, same empty wooden center and genuine transparent background.
Specific damage only: make the existing crack across the ivory skull-shaped helmet somewhat clearer and chip a small corner off its rim; break a noticeable but modest triangular notch from the OUTER edge of the viewer-left shoulder pauldron and let that pauldron hang slightly crooked from one intact strap; fray the lower purple cloth with two larger irregular tears; add one visible split and a chipped end to the viewer-left wooden support foot; give the small round shield a dented brass edge and one split wooden plank. Small scratches elsewhere are okay but prioritize these broad readable damage shapes at small game-sprite scale.
Keep the rack standing and mostly intact, not collapsed or ruined. Preserve the skull's complete recognizable silhouette, both shoulders and both wooden feet; preserve the height, ground contact and transparent margins. No debris scattered outside the original footprint, no blood, no living creature or anatomy, no additional props, no effects, no text, no watermark, no background or floor tile.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target: supplied damaged skeleton-monster armor rack sprite. The user wants SIGNIFICANTLY MORE VISIBLE DAMAGE than this version, especially when reduced to 70 pixels tall in a game. Do not just add scratches. Remove large readable chunks and create an unmistakable battered silhouette while retaining an upright wooden equipment stand.
Keep: same transparent background, same isometric view, same warm painterly stylized 3D art, same object overall size and ground contact, same ivory skull helmet, aged brass/dark iron armor, purple cloth, brown wooden T-frame, no living character.
Required larger damage:
1. Skull-shaped empty helmet: a large jagged missing piece from its upper-right cranium, approximately one quarter of the dome; show the dark hollow interior. Keep the eye sockets and teeth readable as a skull emblem. Large branching crack across the forehead.
2. Viewer-left shoulder armor: half the outer shell has broken away; remaining gold rim is jagged and the remnant dangles diagonally from a visibly frayed strap. Expose the end of the cracked wooden crossbar.
3. Viewer-right shoulder armor: a deep dent and one obvious broad chipped notch along the upper edge.
4. Round wooden shield: one large open split dividing the planks; remove a substantial wedge from the lower-right edge, with two short broken boards and a bent interrupted brass rim. It still leans against the stand.
5. Purple cloth: mostly reduced to two torn narrow hanging strips, big transparent holes and ragged ends rather than merely small fraying.
6. Wooden stand: visibly split crossbar and a broken jagged tip on one foot, with the main post leaning slightly but remaining upright and stable.
No scattered rubble outside the original footprint, no extra objects or weapons, no scene, no tile, no floor, no shadow halo, no text, no blood, no living creature. The damage is on equipment and wood, not anatomy. Preserve generous transparent margins and genuine alpha. Output a single full transparent sprite.
